newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine Justice Minister Jassan quits - sources.
newsitem.headline: Argentine Justice Minister Jassan quits - sources.

text.p: Argentine Justice Minister Elias Jassan has resigned in a scandal over government contacts with a business tycoon being investigated in the murder of a journalist, government sources said on Tuesday.
The scandal snowballed last week after the minister, who had denied contacts with Alfredo Yabran, admitted to having talked to him many times.

Jassan offered his resignation late on Monday to Peronist President Carlos Menem, who was in New York for a United Nations conference, after making what one government source described as a "hardly convincing" defence of his conduct.

The fate of another cabinet minister who newspapers reported was in contact with Yabran, Interior Minister Carlos Corach, remained unclear. Newspapers reported this week Menem will shuffle his cabinet to remove both Jassan and Corach.

Thousands of motorists in Buenos Aires honked their horns in an opposition-sponsored protest against a morning meeting between Yabran and Cabinet Chief Jorge Rodriguez in the Casa Rosada government house.
Dozens of protesters shouted insults at Yabran and broke his automobile's rear windscreen after he left the 40-minute meeting with the senior cabinet minister.
"Thief," several protesters shouted as they kicked the car while Yabran sat calmly in the back seat. Some chanted "assassin, assassin."
The cabinet chief said later that during their meeting Yabran expressed concern over what he described as a "defamation campaign" that was damaging his businesses.

A former policeman was arrested for the killing of Noticias newsmagazine photographer Jose Luis Cabezas in January at a beach resort. But police say Yabran is their "only lead" as to who ordered the murder.
A television journalist investigating the murder said late on Monday his sister was slashed with a razor blade by three thugs as a warning to him to drop the story.

For two years, Yabran has been at the heart of allegations of corruption and money laundering in the government. Former Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo has publicly accused Yabran of leading a mafia with links to the administration.
Official denials that Yabran has been in contact with the government crumbled last week when Corach and Jassan both admitted they received telephone calls from him.

Menem has offered the justice portfolio to Argentina's ambassador to the United States, Raul Granillo Ocampo, one official source said. But another source said the president was also considering other officials for the post.
In July 1996, Jassan replaced Rodolfo Barra, who was forced to resign amid charges he had engaged in neo-Nazi activities in his youth.
